question.text: Affirmative rights differ from veto rights in that:

answer.text: Affirmative rights require shareholders' approval regardless of shareholding percentage, while veto rights oppose a corporate action even if it has the requisite majority
Affirmative rights apply only to debt financing; veto rights apply only to equity financing
Affirmative rights are time-bound to 3 years, while veto rights are perpetual
Affirmative rights are disclosed in PPM while veto rights are only in side letters

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.4 (Affirmative and Veto Rights), affirmative rights are 'positive control' — matters that require investor approval regardless of shareholding size, even if doable via ordinary resolution. Veto rights are 'negative control' — the right to oppose a corporate action even if it has the requisite majority. The Trap: Options B, C, D invent distinctions not in the chapter. The core difference is positive (approval-required) vs negative (block-power) control.
